templates.name: Contrast: established view or appearance, then a finding that breaks it
Contrast: positive claim, then a limiting fact about the same subject
Concession: grant, then the main claim resumes (but / Still)
Concession: supported claim, then a fact that qualifies it
Cause/effect: condition, principle or evidence, then its consequence
Cause/effect: need or judgment, then the action it motivates
Purpose and aptness: goal then deliberate act, or a fitting echo
Addition/similarity: a further item of the same kind
Example: general claim, then one named instance
Specification/restatement: exact content or plain rewording
Emphasis: stronger same-direction fact (content-contrast trap at hard)
Sequence/time: next step, earlier or later event, end of a long effort
Culmination, alternative and place (ultimately, alternatively, there)

items.subtype: Contrast: two subjects, opposite values (sentence-initial)
items.passage: Psychologist Asifa Majid and linguist Niclas Burenhult asked speakers of Jahai, a hunter-gatherer language of the Malay Peninsula, to name a series of odors. The Jahai speakers responded concisely and consistently, using abstract smell terms. ______ English speakers given the same odors offered long, varied descriptions, typically naming a likely source of the smell.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence says the Jahai speakers named the odors briefly and consistently. The last sentence says English speakers given the same odors produced long, varied descriptions. The two groups respond in opposite ways to the same task, so “By contrast” is the logical transition.

A.why_wrong: The English speakers did not respond the way the Jahai speakers did; their answers were long and varied, not concise.

C.why_wrong: The English speakers’ long descriptions are not an instance of the Jahai speakers’ concise naming; they are its opposite.

D.why_wrong: The Jahai speakers’ concise answers did not cause the English speakers to give long descriptions.

sources.what: Majid (psychologist, Radboud University Nijmegen) and Burenhult (linguist, Lund University); Jahai, a hunter-gatherer language of the Malay Peninsula; Jahai and matched English speakers given the same odors; English odor responses about five times longer, mostly source-based descriptions, while Jahai used abstract smell terms
Majid and Burenhult (2014), Odors are expressible in language, as long as you speak the right language, Cognition 130(2)

items.notes: Position: sentence-initial (as in 1.17). The medium C1 item keeps the interrupter, so the two C1 items no longer share a frame.

fixes: subtype label said "interrupter after the subject" but the blank opens the sentence; label corrected

items.replaced: Venus’s slow rotation vs Jupiter (duplicate of command_of_evidence.Q1_P67_criterion.hard)
items.rewrite: new subject (Jahai vs English odor naming, Majid and Burenhult 2014) replacing the redwood and dwarf willow superlatives; blank moved to sentence start

items.subtype: Contrast: established view, then a finding that breaks it
items.passage: Until 2013, rings had been observed only around the solar system’s four giant planets. Few astronomers expected to find them around anything much smaller. ______ that year, a team led by Felipe Braga-Ribas of Brazil’s National Observatory detected two narrow rings encircling Chariklo, an object only about 250 kilometers across that orbits the Sun between Saturn and Uranus.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first two sentences say rings were known only around the giant planets and that few astronomers expected them around much smaller objects. The last sentence reports that a team found rings around Chariklo, an object only about 250 kilometers across. This finding goes against the expectation, so “However” is the logical transition.

A.why_wrong: The expectation that small objects lack rings does not lead to the discovery of rings around one; the discovery goes against it.

B.why_wrong: The discovery does not continue the earlier pattern; it breaks the pattern of rings appearing only around giant planets.

C.why_wrong: The last sentence reports a new discovery; it does not reword what astronomers expected.

sources.what: before Chariklo, rings known only around Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune and none around smaller objects; Chariklo about 250 km across, orbits between Saturn and Uranus; two narrow rings found during the 3 June 2013 occultation; team led by Felipe Braga-Ribas (Observatório Nacional, Rio de Janeiro), who said the team did not think small bodies like Chariklo had rings at all

items.notes: “Few astronomers expected” rests on Braga-Ribas’s own statement that his team did not think small bodies had rings, and on ESO’s note that no rings had been found around smaller objects.
items.rewrite: new subject (Chariklo’s rings, Braga-Ribas 2014) replacing the Great Wall myth; expectation stated as a pattern, not the ‘long been thought’ frame of 1.1

items.subtype: Contrast: a positive claim, then a limiting fact about the same subject
items.passage: Chinese American cinematographer James Wong Howe, renowned for his mastery of shadow and his pioneering use of deep focus, was among Hollywood’s most sought-after camera artists in the 1930s and early 1940s. ______ he was graylisted after being named in testimony as a Communist sympathizer, and he struggled to find work until director Samuel Fuller hired him in 1950.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence says Howe was one of Hollywood’s most sought-after cinematographers. The next says that after he was named as a Communist sympathizer, he was graylisted and had trouble finding work. This setback runs against the success described first, so “However” is the logical transition.

B.why_wrong: Being graylisted and unable to find work is not an example of being sought after; it is the opposite.

C.why_wrong: Howe’s struggle to find work is not similar to his earlier success.

D.why_wrong: Howe’s skill and popularity did not cause him to be named in testimony or graylisted.

sources.what: one of the most sought-after cinematographers in Hollywood in the 1930s and 1940s; master of shadow and one of the first to use deep-focus cinematography; graylisted, named in testimony as a sympathizer, trouble finding work until Samuel Fuller hired him
The Baron of Arizona (1950), directed by Samuel Fuller, photographed by James Wong Howe

items.notes: No time word among the options: “Later” could be argued, since the graylisting came after the success.

fixes: sentence frame copied from official 1.10 (“In the [decade], [person] was [famous] ... ______ [despite/after phrase], [surname] ...”) replaced: the decade moves to the end of the first sentence and the blank sentence opens with its subject

items.rewrite: new subject (James Wong Howe graylisted until Fuller hired him) replacing the Vasa; no figures piled up

items.subtype: Cause/effect: condition, then its consequence
items.passage: In 2006, bicycles were almost never used for everyday travel in Seville, Spain. Between 2006 and 2010, the city built a continuous network of bike lanes physically separated from motorized traffic. ______ bicycle use in Seville rose about sixfold by 2011, according to an analysis by researchers at the University of Seville.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The text says cycling was almost unknown in Seville in 2006 and that the city then built a continuous network of separated bike lanes. The last sentence gives the outcome: bicycle use rose about sixfold. Because the rise follows from the new network, “As a result” is the logical transition.

A.why_wrong: “Regardless” would mean the bike lanes had nothing to do with the rise in cycling, but the rise is the outcome of the new network.

B.why_wrong: The sixfold rise is not an example of building bike lanes; it is what followed from them.

D.why_wrong: The rise in bicycle use is not a similar action to building the network; it is its effect.

sources.what: Marqués, Hernández-Herrador and Calvo-Salazar (SIBUS, University of Sevilla): cycling grew from a negligible share of trips in 2006; continuous network of segregated cycle paths developed 2006 to 2010; bicycle use increased by a factor of about 6 in 2006 to 2011
full text of the same paper (The Sustainable City IX)

items.rewrite: new subject (Seville’s segregated cycle network, Marqués et al.) replacing the Great Salt Lake chain; result attributed to the researchers

items.subtype: Cause/effect: a need, then the action it motivates
items.passage: Scientists studying Antarctica’s Thwaites Glacier wanted measurements from its grounding zone, where the glacier lifts off the seafloor and begins to float. That zone, however, lies beneath hundreds of meters of ice. ______ in early 2020, a team that included astrobiologist Britney Schmidt lowered Icefin, a small robotic submersible, through a hole drilled nearly 600 meters down to the ocean below.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The text says scientists wanted measurements from the grounding zone of Thwaites Glacier but that the zone lies under hundreds of meters of ice. The last sentence describes how a team dealt with this: it drilled through the ice and lowered a robot into the ocean. The ice is the reason for this method, so “For this reason” is the logical transition.

B.why_wrong: Lowering Icefin through a borehole is not being compared or contrasted with the ice; it is how the team got past the ice.

C.why_wrong: Lowering a robot through the ice is not similar to the zone lying under ice; it is a response to that problem.

D.why_wrong: The last sentence describes a new action, not a rewording of the fact that the zone lies under the ice.

sources.what: Icefin, a small robotic oceanographer, deployed through a nearly 2,000-foot-deep borehole; observations near the Thwaites grounding line collected in early 2020; Britney Schmidt, Cornell associate professor
January 2020: Icefin swam from the drill site to the Thwaites grounding zone, where the glacier meets the sea; hole made by the British Antarctic Survey hot-water drill
Britney Schmidt, earth scientist and astrobiologist; at Georgia Tech 2013 to 2021, at Cornell from 2021 (so not a Cornell scientist in early 2020)

items.notes: No concession decoy: “Nevertheless” could be argued (the team reached the zone despite the ice).

fixes: “Cornell University scientist” was anachronistic: in early 2020 Schmidt was at Georgia Tech (she joined Cornell in 2021); now “astrobiologist Britney Schmidt” (source en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Britney_Schmidt)

items.rewrite: new subject (Icefin lowered under Thwaites Glacier, 2020) replacing the Dostoevsky anecdote; key is the longest option

items.subtype: Purpose: a goal, then the deliberate act that serves it
items.passage: In architect Takaharu Tezuka’s view, ordinary classrooms, closed off and tightly controlled, are unnatural places for young children to learn and play. ______ in designing Fuji Kindergarten in suburban Tokyo, he divided the classrooms with stackable wooden boxes instead of walls and turned the building’s oval roof into a playground where children can run laps.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence gives Tezuka’s view that closed, tightly controlled classrooms are unnatural places for young children. The second describes design choices that open the school up: boxes instead of walls and a roof where children can run. These choices put his view into practice, so “With this in mind” is the logical transition.

A.why_wrong: “Nevertheless” would mean Tezuka’s design went against his view, but it follows from it.

B.why_wrong: The second sentence describes specific design choices; it does not restate Tezuka’s view.

C.why_wrong: The second sentence is not a conclusion that sums up the text; it describes what Tezuka did.

sources.what: Fuji Kindergarten in the Tachikawa suburb of Tokyo, completed by Tezuka Architects about 2007; Tezuka considers standard classroom design unnatural and counterproductive (children ‘cannot live in a clean, quiet and controlled environment’); stackable wooden boxes instead of dividing walls; oval rooftop deck used as playground and running track
oval kindergarten in Tokyo erected in 2007; children race around the roof

items.notes: Purpose key: no cause/effect decoy, following the bank’s exclusion rule.
items.rewrite: new subject (Tezuka’s Fuji Kindergarten) replacing Louis Braille; the goal is the architect’s stated view, not the ‘wanted ... With this in mind’ frame of 1.21; key is the longest option

items.subtype: Addition: a second, independent act by the same person
items.passage: Pura Belpré joined the New York Public Library in 1921 as a Spanish-speaking assistant at a branch in Harlem, becoming the first Puerto Rican the library had hired. She started bilingual story hours, often performing Puerto Rican folktales with handmade puppets. ______ she bought Spanish-language books for the library and organized celebrations of Three Kings Day.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The text says Belpré, the library’s first Puerto Rican hire, started bilingual story hours with puppets. The last sentence names more things she did for the same readers: buying Spanish-language books and organizing Three Kings Day celebrations. Because these are further actions of the same kind, “In addition” is the logical transition.

A.why_wrong: Belpré did not buy books and organize celebrations in place of the story hours; she did both.

C.why_wrong: Buying books and organizing celebrations are new actions, not a rewording of the story hours.

D.why_wrong: Nothing in the story hours is being set aside; the new actions serve the same readers.

sources.what: hired in 1921 at the 135th Street branch in Harlem; first Puerto Rican hired by the NYPL; bilingual story hours, buying Spanish-language books, programs for traditional holidays including Three Kings Day; puppeteer

Spanish-speaking assistant at the 135th Street branch; bilingual storytelling programs; performed with handmade puppets; selected Spanish-language children’s books; hosted the first El día de reyes program
told stories with puppets in Spanish and English; the folktale Pérez y Martina

items.notes: Addition key: no similarity decoy.
items.rewrite: new subject (Pura Belpré at the NYPL) replacing Banneker; no padding clause

items.subtype: Example: a general claim, then one named instance
items.passage: Many artists working in West Africa today transform discarded consumer goods into monumental works. ______ Ghanaian artist Serge Attukwei Clottey cuts up yellow plastic jerrycans, which were originally used to transport cooking oil and later to store water during shortages, and stitches the pieces together with copper wire into huge wall hangings.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence makes a general claim: many West African artists turn discarded goods into large works. The second describes one such artist, Clottey, who turns used plastic jerrycans into huge wall hangings. Because Clottey’s work is an instance of the general claim, “For example” is the logical transition.

A.why_wrong: Clottey’s work does not differ from what the first sentence describes; it fits it.

B.why_wrong: The general trend does not cause Clottey to make his hangings; his work is one case of the trend.

D.why_wrong: The second sentence introduces a specific case; it does not sum up the text.

sources.what: Kufuor gallons (jerrycans) first brought to Ghana to transport cooking oil, now used to haul water; nine-foot pieces made from their scraps
yellow plastic Kufuor gallons stitched together using copper wire; they recall Ghana’s mid-2000s water shortages
Afrogallonism: Clottey cuts the containers into small squares and joins them into large works

items.notes: Example key: no specification decoy.
items.replaced: English words borrowed from Arabic, algebra (duplicate of command_of_evidence.Q1_P3_pairwise.medium)
items.rewrite: new subject (Serge Attukwei Clottey’s jerrycan works) replacing serotinous lodgepole cones

items.subtype: Specification: a general statement, then its exact content
items.passage: Native American jewelry, pottery, and baskets are often copied by non-Native makers. The Indian Arts and Crafts Act of 1990, a truth-in-advertising law, governs how such products may be marketed. ______ the act prohibits offering or selling any art or craft product in a manner that falsely suggests it was made by a member of a federally or state-recognized tribe.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence says the Indian Arts and Crafts Act governs how Native American art and craft products may be marketed. The last sentence states exactly what the act requires: a product may not be sold in a way that falsely suggests a tribal member made it. Because it spells out the general statement, “Specifically” is the logical transition.

B.why_wrong: The ban on false claims does not contrast with the act’s role in governing marketing; it is that role.

C.why_wrong: The last sentence does not describe a second, similar law; it explains the same act.

D.why_wrong: “Meanwhile” would introduce something happening at the same time, but the last sentence explains the act already mentioned.

sources.what: Indian Arts and Crafts Act of 1990 (P.L. 101-644), a truth-in-advertising law; illegal to offer or display for sale, or sell, any art or craft product in a manner that falsely suggests it is Indian produced; Indian means a member of a federally or officially State recognized tribe or a tribally certified artisan; jewelry, pottery and baskets among items frequently copied by non-Indians

items.notes: Specification key: no example decoy. The certified-artisan clause of the definition is left out (simplified, not changed).
items.rewrite: new subject (Indian Arts and Crafts Act) replacing Mae Jemison; opening sentence on imitation gives the passage a point beyond the transition; key is the longest option

items.subtype: Emphasis: a claim, then a stronger fact in the same direction
items.passage: The Epic of Manas, about a legendary Kyrgyz hero and his descendants, is traditionally recited by performers called manaschis. Sayakbay Karalaev was renowned among them for the scope of his performances. ______ the version written down from his recitations contains more than 500,000 lines, about twenty times the length of Homer’s Iliad and Odyssey combined.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence says Karalaev was known for the scope of his performances. The last sentence backs this up with a stronger fact: his version of the epic runs to more than 500,000 lines, about twenty times as long as Homer’s two epics. Because it reinforces the previous claim, “In fact” is the logical transition.

A.why_wrong: The length of Karalaev’s version does not replace or contradict his reputation; it supports it.

C.why_wrong: “That said” would introduce a point that limits Karalaev’s reputation, but the line count reinforces it.

D.why_wrong: The text does not describe steps in a process, so nothing comes “next.”

sources.what: Karalaev, perhaps the most famous manaschi, died 1971; the longest recorded version is 500,553 lines, about 20 times the Iliad and Odyssey; manaschi as a traditional reciter of the epic
Karalaev’s variant: 500,553 lines; the two Homeric epics together: 27,803 lines
epic of the hero Manas and his descendants, recited by specialists called manaschi

items.rewrite: new subject (Karalaev’s version of the Epic of Manas) replacing Bach’s cantatas; no gloss of the form

items.subtype: Sequence: the next step of a procedure
items.passage: Seed collections arriving at the Millennium Seed Bank in southern England spend between two weeks and six months in a drying room kept at 15 percent relative humidity. ______ technicians clean the seeds and X-ray them, discarding any that are empty or damaged by insects. Only then are the seeds dried again and transferred to underground vaults kept at −20°C.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The text follows seed collections through the seed bank in order. They are dried for weeks or months, then cleaned and X-rayed, and only after that dried again and moved to the vaults. Cleaning and X-raying is the step that comes after the first drying, so “Next” is the logical transition.

A.why_wrong: Cleaning the seeds is not contrasted with drying them; it is the following step.

B.why_wrong: Cleaning and X-raying are not like drying; they are a different, later step.

D.why_wrong: The second sentence describes a new step; it does not reword the first.

sources.what: Kew’s Millennium Seed Bank at Wakehurst: initial drying room at 15°C and 15% relative humidity for two weeks to six months; then cleaning and X-ray, empty or insect-damaged seeds discarded; then the main drying room; then vaults at −20°C

items.notes: Kew’s page answers 403 to scripts; read through the Wayback Machine copy (web.archive.org/web/2023id_/ plus the same URL).

fixes: subtype label still named the “First ... ______ ... Finally” frame the rewrite removed; label corrected

items.rewrite: new subject (Millennium Seed Bank processing) replacing washi; no First ... Finally frame around the blank

items.subtype: Contrast: two subjects, opposite values (interrupter after the subject)
items.passage: In experiments conducted on Barbados, biologist Jean-Nicolas Audet found that bullfinches captured in heavily urbanized parts of the island excelled at innovative foraging tasks, such as opening a drawer to obtain food, and also mounted vigorous immune responses. Bullfinches from rural habitats, ______ solved such problems less readily and exhibited comparatively weak immunity.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence says urban bullfinches were good at solving foraging problems and had strong immune responses. The second says rural bullfinches did worse on both. The two groups have opposite results on the same measures, so “in contrast” is the logical transition.

A.why_wrong: Rural birds did not perform like urban birds; they solved fewer problems and had weaker immunity.

B.why_wrong: The urban birds’ success does not cause the rural birds’ poorer results.

C.why_wrong: Rural birds are not an example of urban birds excelling; they are the group being compared.

sources.what: urban Barbados bullfinches better at innovative problem-solving tasks such as opening drawers to access food and with better immunity than rural birds; Jean-Nicolas Audet first author; Behavioral Ecology 2016
Audet, Ducatez and Lefebvre, The town bird and the country bird: problem solving and immunocompetence vary with urbanization

items.notes: Position: interrupter after the subject (as in 2.6); the easy C1 item now opens with the blank instead.
items.rewrite: new subject (Audet’s Barbados bullfinches) replacing gamelan; key changed to ‘in contrast’ with a new option set

items.subtype: Contrast: established pattern, then a case that breaks it (interrupter after the subject)
items.passage: In most animals, a beating heart moves blood and oxygen through the body. The hearts of sea spiders, ______ are so feeble that they propel fluid only within the central body; in a 2017 study of twelve species, biologist H. Arthur Woods and colleagues determined that oxygen reaches the animals’ spindly legs chiefly through peristaltic contractions of gut branches extending into each leg.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence states the usual pattern: in most animals, the heart moves blood and oxygen through the body. The second says sea spiders’ hearts are too weak to do this beyond the central body, so their guts do much of the work. Sea spiders are an exception to the pattern, so “however” is the logical transition.

B.why_wrong: The general pattern does not cause sea spiders’ hearts to be weak; sea spiders break the pattern.

C.why_wrong: “Moreover” would add a point supporting the first sentence, but the sea spider case goes against it.

D.why_wrong: The second sentence describes a different case; it does not reword the first.

sources.what: most animals depend on a beating heart; sea spiders’ hearts beat only weakly and moved no blood beyond the central portion; gut branches reach the end of every leg; 12 species studied; H. Arthur Woods, University of Montana
Woods et al. (2017), Respiratory gut peristalsis by sea spiders, Current Biology 27(13)

items.notes: Position: interrupter after the subject (as in 2.16), not after an introductory phrase. Only one adversative option, so “by contrast” is not offered next to the key.

fixes: subtype label said “blank after an introductory phrase”, but the blank is an interrupter after the subject; label corrected

items.rewrite: new subject (Woods’s sea spider gut peristalsis) replacing the lichen third partner; blank moved from after ‘In 2016,’ to an interrupter

items.subtype: Cause/effect: mechanism, then its consequence
items.passage: Because red blood cells absorb green light, circulating blood can betray an otherwise translucent frog resting on a leaf. In 2022, biologists Carlos Taboada and Jesse Delia reported that sleeping glassfrogs remove nearly 90 percent of their red blood cells from circulation and sequester them in the liver. ______ the resting frogs become two to three times more transparent.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence explains that circulating red blood cells can make a translucent frog visible. The second says sleeping glassfrogs pull nearly all of these cells out of circulation and store them in the liver. Becoming more transparent is the effect of hiding the cells, so “Consequently” is the logical transition.

A.why_wrong: Becoming more transparent does not contrast with removing the red blood cells; it follows from it.

C.why_wrong: Greater transparency is not an example of storing blood cells in the liver; it is the result.

D.why_wrong: The frogs’ transparency is not a second, similar behavior; it is the outcome of the first.

sources.what: red blood cells absorb green light; resting glassfrogs removed nearly 90 percent of circulating red blood cells and stored them in the liver; Carlos Taboada (co-first author) and Jesse Delia

Taboada et al. (2022), Glassfrogs conceal blood in their liver to maintain transparency, Science 378: resting frogs two to three times more transparent once about 89 percent of red blood cells leave circulation

items.rewrite: new subject (Taboada and Delia’s glassfrog study) replacing Antarctic fish antifreeze; key changed to Consequently

items.subtype: Cause/effect: a judgment, then the action it motivates
items.passage: After high water on the Rhine and Meuse forced the evacuation of some 250,000 people in 1995, Dutch authorities concluded that continually raising dikes was a losing strategy and that the rivers needed more space to discharge floodwater. ______ the Room for the River program, carried out at 34 locations between 2007 and 2015, moved dikes farther back, excavated high-water channels, and lowered floodplains.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence gives the conclusion Dutch authorities drew after the 1995 floods: the rivers needed more space. The second describes a program that gave them that space by moving dikes back and lowering floodplains. The program acted on the conclusion, so “Accordingly” is the logical transition.

A.why_wrong: “Nevertheless” would mean the program went against the authorities’ conclusion, but it carried it out.

B.why_wrong: The program is not a similar, separate event; it is the action taken because of the conclusion.

D.why_wrong: The program came years after the 1995 conclusion, so the two did not happen at the same time.

sources.what: 1995: protected areas along the Meuse and Rhine threatened, 240,000 people and a million cattle evacuated; the government realized continually strengthening the dikes was a losing proposition; 1996 Room for the River guideline; 2006 planning decision for 34 projects

in 1995, 250,000 people and a million animals evacuated; rivers given more room at 34 locations; start 2007, completion 2015; measures include floodplain excavation, dike relocation and high-water channels

items.notes: Sources give 240,000 or 250,000 evacuated; the passage says “some 250,000”.

fixes: “lowered floodplains at 34 locations” implied floodplain lowering at all 34 sites; the 34 locations now qualify the whole program (UNESCO-IHE brochure: room at 34 locations with a mix of measures)

items.replaced: Francis Kéré’s Pritzker and Gando school (duplicate of central_ideas_and_details.T3.medium)
items.rewrite: new subject (Dutch Room for the River program) replacing the Great Stink; motive is a policy conclusion, not a vivid anecdote

items.subtype: Aptness: a notable fact, then a fitting echo of it
items.passage: Since 1999, the Fourth Plinth in London’s Trafalgar Square has displayed a rotating series of commissions by contemporary artists. The square commemorates Horatio Nelson’s 1805 naval victory at Trafalgar, and his statue presides over it from atop a monumental column. ______ British Nigerian artist Yinka Shonibare’s 2010 commission was a scale replica of Nelson’s flagship, HMS Victory, sealed inside a giant bottle.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The text says that Trafalgar Square commemorates Nelson’s victory at Trafalgar and that his statue looks over the square. Shonibare’s commission for the square’s plinth was a replica of Nelson’s own flagship. A work about Nelson’s ship suits a square built to honor Nelson, so “Fittingly” is the logical transition.

A.why_wrong: “Regardless” would mean the square’s link to Nelson has no bearing on the commission, but the commission matches that link exactly.

C.why_wrong: The last sentence does not reword the description of the square; it introduces a new fact about a particular artwork.

D.why_wrong: Nothing about the replica of Nelson’s flagship is the reverse of the square’s tribute to Nelson; the two facts agree.

sources.what: Fourth Plinth built 1841 for an equestrian statue (William IV), left empty; first contemporary work in 1999; Nelson’s Ship in a Bottle shown 24 May 2010 to January 2012
square named to commemorate the 1805 Battle of Trafalgar; statue of Nelson at the top of Nelson’s Column
1:30 scale replica of HMS Victory in a bottle, commissioned for the Fourth Plinth
Shonibare, British Nigerian artist; Victory as Nelson’s flagship; bottle size

items.notes: Aptness: the setting is described first and the fitting choice follows (the official 2.5 runs the other way, from a poem to the name of its school). Sentence-initial blank.

fixes: cut the equestrian-statue aside (trivia the question never uses) and said instead that the plinth shows a rotating series of commissions; 65 words, above the official medium maximum of 62, down to 61

items.replaced: Ada Lovelace and the Ada language (duplicate of rhetorical_synthesis.QUOTE.hard)
items.rewrite: New subject (Shonibare’s Fourth Plinth ship replaces Sojourner Truth); aptness built from setting to fitting commission, no name-echo or gloss; denser register; decoys changed.

items.subtype: Addition: a second method used for the same goal
items.passage: Conservation biologist Samuel Wasser traces ivory trafficking by comparing DNA from confiscated tusks with a genetic reference map built from samples of elephant dung, skin, and hair collected across Africa, an approach that reveals where poaching is concentrated. ______ his team searches separate seizures for the two tusks of a single elephant: a match indicates that both shipments originated with the same dealer.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence describes one way Wasser’s team tracks ivory: matching tusk DNA to a reference map to find where elephants were killed. The second sentence describes a second, separate technique: finding the two tusks of one elephant in different seizures to link the shipments to one dealer. Because the second sentence adds another method to the first, “In addition” is the logical transition.

A.why_wrong: “Granted” would concede a point that limits the first sentence, but matching tusks is not a weakness of the mapping method; it is another tool.

B.why_wrong: Searching seizures for paired tusks is not a rewording of comparing DNA with a reference map; it is a different technique with a different result.

C.why_wrong: “Instead” would mean the team uses tusk matching in place of the reference map, but the text presents both as methods the team uses.

sources.what: Wasser et al. 2015, Science: DNA from 28 large seizures compared with 1,350 reference samples of dung, skin and hair from 29 African countries, revealing two poaching hotspots
reference samples from dung, skin and hair; poaching hotspots

items.subtype: Restatement: a technical term, then a plain definition (after an em dash)
items.passage: In a 2016 study, plant biologist Stacey Harmer and her colleagues showed that a circadian clock controls heliotropism in young sunflowers—______ the plants’ stems bend over the course of each day so that the buds follow the Sun from east to west. Once the flowers mature, however, they stop moving and face east.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: “Heliotropism” is a technical term. The words after the dash explain what it means: the stems bend so the buds follow the Sun. Because this part restates the term in plain language, “that is” is the logical transition.

B.why_wrong: The bending stems do not happen in spite of heliotropism; they are what heliotropism is.

C.why_wrong: The bending is not a separate event happening at the same time as heliotropism; it is heliotropism.

D.why_wrong: The description adds no new finding; it explains the term just used.

items.subtype: Time: the end of a long effort
items.passage: Rearing Pacific bluefin tuna from the eggs of captive-raised parents defeated many research institutes: in hatchery tanks, larvae cannibalized one another, and juveniles frequently died after colliding with the walls. Japan’s Kindai University, which began investigating the species in 1970, persisted after other programs had abandoned the effort. ______ in 2002, its researchers produced the world’s first fully farm-raised bluefin.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The text describes a long struggle: many institutes failed to rear bluefin tuna from captive-bred parents, and Kindai kept working on the problem from 1970 after others gave up. The last sentence gives the success that came at the end of that effort in 2002. “Finally” marks the end of a long process, so it is the logical transition.

A.why_wrong: The 2002 success is not one example of Kindai’s persistence or of the difficulties; it is the result reached at the end of them.

B.why_wrong: The success is not like the failures described earlier; it is what came after them.

D.why_wrong: Producing the first fully farm-raised bluefin in 2002 does not reword the claim that Kindai persisted; it adds a new event.

items.subtype: Place: B happens at the place just named
items.passage: Cosmic rays, which continuously bombard Earth’s surface, generate background signals that can obscure the exceedingly rare particle interactions sought by dark matter experiments. China’s Jinping Underground Laboratory, inaugurated in 2010 midway along a road tunnel in Sichuan Province, lies beneath 2,400 meters of marble; ______ the PandaX experiment monitors liquid xenon for the faint recoil of atomic nuclei struck by dark matter particles.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first clause names a place, the Jinping Underground Laboratory deep under a mountain, and the clause after the semicolon tells what happens at that place: the PandaX experiment looks for dark matter. “There” points back to the place just named, so it is the logical transition.

B.why_wrong: Nothing is being compared: the PandaX experiment is not set against the laboratory’s depth but carried out inside it.

C.why_wrong: The clause about PandaX does not sum up what came before; it adds a new fact about what the laboratory is used for.

D.why_wrong: “Nevertheless” would mean the experiment runs in spite of the laboratory’s depth, but the depth is what shields it from cosmic rays.

items.subtype: Contrast: two positions on one question (blank after an introductory phrase)
items.passage: Surveying birds and trees in Ghana and India, Ben Phalan and colleagues concluded in 2011 that most species fare best when crops are grown intensively on minimal land, leaving more forest intact. For ecologists Ivette Perfecto and John Vandermeer, ______ what matters most is not how much forest is spared but the quality of the farmland between forest fragments, through which species must migrate to survive.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: Phalan and colleagues conclude that most species do best when farming is intensive and confined to as little land as possible, so that more forest is spared. Perfecto and Vandermeer hold that what matters most is not the amount of forest spared but the quality of the farmland between forest fragments. These are opposing answers to the same question, so “by contrast” is the logical transition.

A.why_wrong: Perfecto and Vandermeer’s view does not follow from Phalan’s findings; it rejects the idea that sparing forest is what matters most.

B.why_wrong: “Moreover” would add a point that supports Phalan’s conclusion, but Perfecto and Vandermeer put the quality of farmland ahead of the amount of forest spared, the opposite emphasis.

C.why_wrong: The last sentence does not reword Phalan’s conclusion; it gives other researchers’ competing view.

items.subtype: Contrast: a claim about one side of a figure’s work, then a fact about the same work that pulls against it (interrupter after the subject)
items.passage: Malian singer Oumou Sangaré built her sound on wassoulou, a style rooted in the pentatonic songs of her mother’s home region in southern Mali and anchored by the kamalengoni, a harp derived from the instrument played by Wassoulou hunters. Her lyrics, ______ have challenged social conventions long accepted there: her 1989 debut album, Moussolou (“Women”), warned listeners against polygamy and forced marriage.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence stresses how closely Sangaré’s music follows the tradition of the Wassoulou region. The next sentence turns to her lyrics, which challenge conventions long accepted in that same region. Because the lyrics pull against the tradition the music draws on, the contrast word “though” is the logical transition.

A.why_wrong: Building her sound on a regional tradition does not lead her to challenge that region’s customs; the two facts pull in opposite directions.

C.why_wrong: Her lyrics are not an example of a sound rooted in Wassoulou tradition; they are a different part of her work that departs from tradition.

D.why_wrong: “Likewise” would mean the lyrics resemble the music, but the music follows tradition while the lyrics challenge it.

items.subtype: Concession: an obvious objection granted, then the claim resumes with “Still”
items.passage: The paintings that senior men began producing in 1971 at Papunya, a settlement in Australia’s Western Desert, extended a visual tradition far older than the settlement itself. ______ their medium was new: the acrylic paints distributed by schoolteacher Geoffrey Bardon and the scraps of building board they painted on had no precedent in the region’s art. Yet the designs came from ceremonial body painting and sand mosaics.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence claims that the Papunya paintings continued a very old tradition. The second sentence admits a point against that claim: the paints and boards were new. The last sentence (“Yet ...”) returns to the main claim: the designs came from old ceremonies. A writer who grants a point before turning back to the claim uses “Admittedly,” so it is the logical transition.

A.why_wrong: The paintings’ link to an old tradition is not the reason their materials were new.

B.why_wrong: “Moreover” would add support for the first sentence, but new materials cut against the claim of continuity; the “Yet” that follows shows the sentence is a concession.

D.why_wrong: New paints and boards are not a more precise statement of the old tradition the first sentence describes; they are a point against it.

items.subtype: Concession: a supported claim, then a fact that qualifies it
items.passage: Because white light-emitting diodes (LEDs) are more energy efficient than the yellow high-pressure sodium lamps long used to light roads, municipalities worldwide are converting their streetlights to LEDs. ______ the transition may intensify the ecological effects of light pollution. In a 2014 study, Stephen Pawson and Martin Bader found that LED-fitted light traps captured, on average, 48 percent more insects than traps with sodium lamps.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence gives a good reason for switching streetlights to LEDs: they save energy. The next sentence limits that picture: the switch may make light pollution worse for wildlife, as a 2014 study of insects suggests. A transition that accepts a point and then adds a qualification is needed, so “That said” is the logical choice.

A.why_wrong: Saving energy does not cause the ecological harm; the harm comes from the light itself, as the study shows.

C.why_wrong: The ecological cost is not similar to the energy savings; it is a drawback that weighs against them.

D.why_wrong: The possible harm to insects is not a conclusion drawn from the energy savings; it qualifies them.

items.subtype: Cause/effect: evidence, then the conclusion it licenses (after a semicolon)
items.passage: In 2014, a team led by Morten Allentoft analyzed ancient DNA from 281 moa, the giant flightless birds that vanished from New Zealand after Polynesian settlement in the late thirteenth century. In all four species studied, the DNA revealed large populations whose genetic diversity held steady for the 4,000 years before the extinction; ______ people, not a prior decline, most likely drove the birds to extinction.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The DNA study found that moa populations stayed large and genetically stable right up to the extinction, which followed Polynesian settlement. That evidence rules out a decline already under way and points to people as the cause. The clause after the semicolon draws this conclusion from the evidence, so “therefore” is the logical transition.

B.why_wrong: The conclusion about what caused the extinction is not a second, similar finding; it is drawn from the DNA evidence.

C.why_wrong: “Nevertheless” would mean the conclusion holds in spite of the evidence, but the large, stable populations are exactly what rule out a prior decline.

D.why_wrong: The clause does not describe something happening at the same time as the study; it draws a conclusion from the study’s results.

items.subtype: Purpose: a belief or goal, then the deliberate act that serves it
items.passage: German architect Anna Heringer meant the school she designed for the Bangladeshi village of Rudrapur to serve the local economy as well as its pupils: the construction budget, she argued, should stay with villagers rather than flow to outside industries such as cement manufacturing. ______ the METI school, completed in 2005, was built largely by local craftspeople and villagers from earth, straw, and bamboo.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The first sentence states Heringer’s goal: the money for building the school should stay with the villagers rather than go to outside industries such as cement makers. The second sentence describes what she did to meet that goal: local people built the school from local earth, straw, and bamboo. Because the second sentence is the action taken to serve the goal, “To that end” is the logical transition.

A.why_wrong: “Regardless” would mean Heringer’s goal did not matter to how the school was built, but the building method carries out that goal.

B.why_wrong: Nothing is being compared: the second sentence describes the same school, not a different one.

C.why_wrong: The construction is not a separate event happening alongside Heringer’s goal; it is the way she pursued it.

The second sentence names another strand of the same book: Bui’s own experience as a new mother. Because it adds a further element of the book, “Additionally” is the logical transition.

B.why_wrong: Bui’s own motherhood is not a more exact account of her parents’ lives; it is a separate part of the book.

items.subtype: Restatement: an abstract principle, then a plain rewording
items.passage: Integrative Science, a program launched at Cape Breton University in 1999, sought to combine Indigenous and Western sciences within a single curriculum. In 2004, Mi’kmaw Elder Albert Marshall articulated its guiding principle, Etuaptmumk, or Two-Eyed Seeing. ______ learners were to view the world with one eye attuned to the strengths of Indigenous knowledge and the other attuned to those of Western science, using both perspectives simultaneously.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The second sentence gives the name of a principle, Two-Eyed Seeing, without explaining it. The last sentence explains what the name means: seeing with the strengths of Indigenous knowledge through one eye and of Western science through the other, using both together. Because it restates the principle in plain terms, “That is” is the logical transition.

A.why_wrong: The last sentence does not add a new point to the principle; it explains what the principle itself means.

C.why_wrong: “Instead” would set the last sentence against Two-Eyed Seeing, but it describes Two-Eyed Seeing.

D.why_wrong: The way of seeing described in the last sentence is the 2004 principle itself, not something that came before it.

items.subtype: Emphasis: content-contrast trap (B describes other cases but supports A)
items.passage: In 2021, researchers Lyubov Shmakova and Stas Malavin reported that a bdelloid rotifer, a microscopic freshwater animal, had revived from Siberian permafrost about 24,000 years old and then reproduced in the laboratory. The finding vastly extended the known limits of rotifer survival in a frozen state. ______ earlier reports had documented rotifers surviving for only six to ten years when frozen.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The text claims that the 24,000-year survival vastly extended what was known about how long frozen rotifers can survive. The last sentence gives a fact that makes the claim even stronger: earlier reports showed only six to ten years. Although it describes earlier findings, it supports the claim rather than opposing it, so “In fact” is the logical transition.

B.why_wrong: The short earlier record does not cut against the claim that the finding extended the limits; it shows how large the extension was.

C.why_wrong: The earlier reports came before the 2021 finding, so they cannot be its result.

D.why_wrong: The earlier six-to-ten-year record is not an example of the new finding; it is the old limit the finding surpassed.

items.subtype: Culmination: what happened in the end, with the contrast already marked by “though”
items.passage: Chinese artist Song Dong assembled Waste Not in 2005 from more than 10,000 objects his mother had saved over five decades, hoping the project would ease her grief after his father’s death in 2002. Though it began as a private consolation, ______ the installation came to be seen as a portrait of a generation for whom thrift had been a strategy for surviving decades of political upheaval.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
items.explanation: The text says that Waste Not began as a way to help the artist’s mother through her grief. The sentence with the blank tells what the work became in the end: a portrait of a whole generation. “Though” already marks the contrast between the start and the outcome, so the blank needs a word for the final result, and “ultimately” is the logical transition.

A.why_wrong: The sentence does not add a second, separate point; it tells what the private project turned into over time.

B.why_wrong: Beginning as a private consolation is not the reason the work came to be seen as a portrait of a generation; the “Though” clause presents it as a contrast.

C.why_wrong: The installation’s later reputation is not an example of anything stated before; it is the outcome of the project.
